title: Batch PR grooming notes and micro-refactor backlog
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal scratchpad for batching small PRs (1–3 file changes, low-risk) into review waves. Goal is to reduce reviewer context switching, keep master green, and clear a backlog of tiny refactors and lints that block larger refactors. Not a canonical process — more of a practical checklist + follow-ups I use when triaging my queue.

Quick summary of the pattern I want to try:
- Collect small PRs across the repo into weekly 'micro-groom' bundles (max 8 PRs).
- Prefer merging bundles that have independent changes (no cross-PR conflicts).
- Use a single CI smoke batch job before merging bundle (see commands below).
- For code-style/lint fixes: prefer squash-and-merge with a note in the commit message referencing the original PRs.

Batch inclusion criteria (fast accept):
- < 10 LOC in any single file OR <= 3 small files changed
- No schema/migration or proto changes
- No production config flips (feature flags off by default OK)
- Unit tests or linter touched files AND CI passes on the PR
- Not touching the serving runtime core paths (unless strictly isolated)

Review heuristics for reviewers (short cheat-sheet):
- If it’s a rename / comment / doc update: skim for intent, check references (search for old name)
- If it’s a tiny refactor (extract function, move helper): ensure behavior same via unit tests or simple manual run of the module
- If it modifies interface boundaries: require explicit test or example showing compatibility
- If it touches performance-critical loop: ask for before/after micro-benchmark or rationale

Pre-merge smoke steps (manual run before merging a bundle):
- Checkout branch locally and run unit tests for changed modules only:
  - git fetch origin && git checkout PR_BRANCH
  - tox -e py39 -- tests/path/to/changed_files
- Run local quick serve for affected endpoint(s):
  - docker-compose -f infra/local-compose.yml up --build -d
  - curl -sS "http://localhost:8080/health"
- Run combined linter and static checks: staticcheck, mypy
- Run the bundle-ci script (I have a small helper): ./scripts/bundle-ci --branches pr1 pr2 pr3
  - it will create a temporary multi-PR merge in CI to catch inter-PR conflicts

Merging strategy (bundle):
- Prefer 'squash and merge' for housekeeping PRs with clear commit message summarizing all PRs included.
- For tiny behavioral fixes keep separate commits if changelog needs to attribute author.
- Backport policy: only if issue affects release branch or customer-reported bug. Otherwise leave for next release cycle.

Automation ideas (todo list):
- [ ] Auto-labeler rule: label "micro-groom/ok" when PR meets file/loc thresholds
- [ ] Small server-side script to simulate merged CI across N PRs (improve ./scripts/bundle-ci)
- [ ] Add a GitHub Action step that runs changed-module tests instead of whole repo when possible
- [ ] Dashboard card in Console for "pending micro-prs" count per owner

Common follow-ups I file after merging batch:
- Create a short PR-note in the original PRs linking to the bundle merge commit
- Add a changelog entry if behaviour changed (even tiny) under "internal" section
- Add tasks in the backlog board for any discovered follow-up (performance, docs, e2e)

Edge cases and gotchas (lessons learned):
- Watch for flapping tests that pass locally but fail in CI due to order dependencies — re-run CI with parallelism=1 sometimes reveals order-related failures
- Don't bundle PRs that each rely on a different migration or proto change; merging order will bite you
- When squashing multiple small fixes that touch the same file, keep a note of original authorship in the commit body

Examples (recent decisions):
- PR #2134 (small logging cleanup) was bundled with two lint PRs; we squashed with commit message: "bundle: logging cleanup + lints — refs #2134,#2179" — saved 2 CI cycles.
- I deferred PR #2210 (refactor cache key) because it touched runtime cache API; should be scheduled for dedicated review.

Checklist template I paste into PR comments when proposing a bundle merge:
- Bundle PRs: [#2134], [#2179], [#2190]
- Smoke checks: local tests ✅ / docker health ✅ / bundle-ci run ✅
- Conflict check: merged preview branch built in CI ✅
- Changelog: none / internal note added ✅
- Owner approvals: @owner1 @owner2 ✅

Action items (next time I run a batch):
- Improve bundle-ci to post a combined CI status in PRs automatically (assign to self, 2d)
- Propose auto-label for micro-groom in weekly engineering sync (add to agenda)
- Clean the backlog list in the repo project: move stale items older than 6 months to archived list

Open questions I keep here for discussion:
- Do we want to set an explicit max bundle size? (I lean toward <=8 PRs to keep CI runtime sane)
- How aggressive should backports be for housekeeping PRs? (conservative: only if customer-facing)
- Are reviewers comfortable with a single 'bundle' CI run being considered sufficient QA for these micro changes?

Notes to self (quick commands):
- Create preview merge branch: git checkout -b preview/batch-2025-02 && git merge pr/2134 pr/2179 pr/2190 --no-ff && git push origin preview/batch-2025-02
- Run bundle-ci: ./scripts/bundle-ci preview/batch-2025-02
- Post summary comment linking original PRs and the preview branch

Rough backlog (small/quick wins):
- move-helpers: rename util -> helpers (1 file)
- logging-context: replace print -> structured logger (2 files)
- tests: fix flaky test in tests/inference/test_streaming.py (retry-based)
- docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md with new PR template (1 file)

End of scratchpad. Keep this file as a living note — copy into a proper doc if we decide to make a team-wide micro-grooming playbook.
